head: pr17421-r26
report:
## DEFECT: Cancelling a `/resume` of a session another process owns leaves a fork file behind

**Mechanism.** In `AgentSession.switchSession` (`session/agent-session.ts` ~13245–13268), `setSessionFile(sessionPath, { forkIfContested: true })` runs before the working-directory check. When another live process owns the target, `#adoptLoadedSessionAsFork` creates a new session id and file beside the target. It also starts `copySessionArtifacts` into that fork's artifacts directory and takes a claim. Then `noteResumedSessionFork` appends the `owned-elsewhere` notice and calls `flushEntries()`, which writes the fork to disk.

The cwd check runs only after that. It throws `SESSION_CWD_CHANGE_REJECTED` when the user declines the prompt, or when no `onCwdChange` callback is given (extension and RPC switches into another project). The `catch` then calls `restoreState(previousSessionState)`, which puts the manager back on the original session but never removes the fork. Neither `restoreState` nor the `catch` block in `switchSession` removes the fork file or stops its artifact copy.

So a `/resume` the user refused still leaves a new session in the target project: the owner's whole transcript plus the notice, with `parentSession` naming the owner. Before this patch, `setSessionFile` wrote nothing, so this is new.

**Trigger.** Process A is in project S. Process B (live) owns session T in project P. In A, `/resume` T and answer "no" at the working-directory prompt; or call `switchSession(T)` with no `onCwdChange` while S ≠ P.

**Measured.** I added this probe to a scratch copy of `test/session/session-manager-shared-session-file.test.ts`, using its `liveSession`, `createSession` and `OtherProcess.adopt` helpers. Its steps: target owned by `OtherProcess`, then `switchSession(target, { onCwdChange: async () => false })`.
- `switchSession` returned `false`.
- The manager was back on the source file and id.
- The target directory now held a second `.jsonl`:

```
BEFORE [".../2026-10-31T16-55-52-517Z_01a192e3-9bc5-...79.jsonl"]
AFTER  [".../2026-10-31T16-55-52-517Z_01a192e3-9bc5-...79.jsonl",
        ".../2026-10-31T16-55-54-071Z_01a192e3-a1d7-...52.jsonl"]
NEW FILE {"type":"session","id":"01a192e3-a1d7-...","parentSession":"01a192e3-9bc5-...","cwd":".../omp-probe-target-..."}
TURNS ["target"]
```

**Impact.** The orphan is the newest session in that project. `[INFERENCE]` It will appear in the resume picker, and `--continue` may pick it over the owner's session; I did not run either. Its background artifact copy (and the `noteArtifactsNotReproduced` / `#tellModelWhenArtifactsAreMissing` follow-ups that were started) also keep running after the rollback.

**Fix shape.** Do the cwd and model checks before forking. Or, on rollback, discard a fork this switch created: drop its file and artifacts directory, and cancel or ignore its copy and notices.

## NOT A DEFECT

**Earlier round's findings (astra r24, head `2a21e950`), checked by reading the code at this head.** I did not rerun the earlier probes against this head.

| # | Earlier finding | At this head |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | JS `settledArtifactOf` drops `root` | **Closed.** `artifact-wire.ts` builds the answer from `SETTLED_ARTIFACT_FIELDS`, which includes `root: "optional"`, so `root` crosses the bridge. `helpers.ts` `askArtifact` binds it with `roots[EVAL_ARTIFACT_ROOT_TOKEN] ??= answer.root`. |
| 2 | Pin given back before it is used | **Closed.** JS `readSettledArtifact` and Python `_read_settled_artifact` release only in `finally`, after the read. A read that takes the pin (`taken = true`) skips the release. The Python fallback no longer sends the same token as both `file` and `release`. |
| 3 | Pins outlive finished cells, killed consumers and disposed sessions | **Closed in code; not re-measured.** Each JS run (`invokeJsTool`/`runOnce`) and each Python run entry gets its own `ArtifactPinOwner`, and `.end()` runs when the run ends. Kernel-level pins end in `killSession` and `unregisterPyToolBridgeSession`. `AgentSession.#doDispose` calls `releaseArtifactPinsOf`. Every pin also has a 2 s timer that releases it unprompted. |
| 4 | Expiry decrements the quota count twice | **Closed.** The count is now `accounts: Map<string, Set<ArtifactPin>>`. `ArtifactPin.take()` removes the pin from the token table, its account and its owner in one step, and it can only succeed once. |
| 5 | Fallback reads charge the source owner's quota | **Closed.** Pins are charged to `pinAccountOf(session)`, the session doing the reading, whichever directory the file was found in. |
| 6 | Two consumers read one pin and get different bytes | **Closed.** `takePinnedArtifact` calls the synchronous `pin.take()` before any await, so a second consumer gets "no longer held open". |
| — | Publication-lock waits use `Date.now()` | Not in this patch's scope: the earlier report itself says those lines match upstream. |

**Other things I checked and ruled out:**
- **`session_moved` delivery.** `AgentSession` emits it through `#extensionRunner.emit`. The runner lists it in `SESSION_IDENTITY_EVENTS`, and both the extension and hook `on()` overloads accept it. The SDK custom-tool bridge (`sdk.ts`), autoresearch and warp-events all subscribe to it. Nothing drops it.
- **Every `captureState()` caller ends its snapshot claim.** `switchSession` commits on success and restores in `catch`. Both `/move` paths (`command-controller.ts`, `builtin-lifecycle.ts`) commit in `finally`. `cloneCurrentSession` commits at once. I found no leaked claim.
- **Same-file reload with `forkIfContested`.** The process's own lease is refcounted, so reloading its own session never reads as "owned elsewhere".

The probe is in the scratch directory: `orphan-fork.test.ts`, run with `-t PROBE` from `packages/coding-agent`. A `node_modules` symlink there points at the snapshot's install so imports resolve.
